methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $6M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Albacore is a Seed-stage ocean and maritime technology company founded by John Huddleston and Dante Vaisbort. The company has raised $6.5M to date. The comparable universe consists of three private peers in the ocean and maritime sector—Standard Subsea, Clippership, and NetworkOcean—as no directly comparable public companies trade in this space.

Stage-progression methodology is applicable to this valuation. Using total capital raised ($6.5M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $16.25M. This method reflects the capital-efficiency expectations and de-risking associated with progression from Seed to Series A financing.

The triangulation analysis, constrained by available methodological applicability, supports a valuation range of $13.8M to $18.7M, with a median of $16M. This range reflects upside and downside scenarios around the stage-progression base case. The primary limitations on precision are the single applicable methodology and the immature public comparables set in ocean tech, creating material uncertainty around sustainable revenue multiples and category-specific risk premia. Validation of this range would benefit from primary data on the three private peer financings and clearer line-of-sight to Albacore's near-term revenue trajectory.
